_note: Passage texts are short paraphrased excerpts written to stand in for the public source documents. Before the main sweep, replace each one with the verbatim text from source_url at the given locator, check every gold answer in questions.json against it, then freeze both files in Git. `ingest` holds the date/version/status that ingestion can read off the document itself (shown in arm A2 only). Families with default_pool=true contribute distractor passages to questions from other families.

passages.locator: Line 12, Standard Deduction Chart for Most People
passages.text: 2024 Form 1040 Instructions, Line 12. Standard Deduction Chart for Most People. If your filing status is Single or Married filing separately, your standard deduction is $14,600. Married filing jointly or Qualifying surviving spouse: $29,200. Head of household: $21,900. Do not use this chart if you were born before January 2, 1960, or were blind, or if someone can claim you as a dependent.

passages.locator: Line 12, Standard Deduction Chart for People Born Before January 2, 1960, or Blind
passages.text: 2024 Form 1040 Instructions. If you were born before January 2, 1960, or were blind at the end of 2024, you get an additional standard deduction. The additional amount for each condition is $1,950 if you are unmarried (Single or Head of household), or $1,550 if you are married or a qualifying surviving spouse.

passages.locator: Schedule 1, Line 21, Student Loan Interest Deduction
passages.text: 2024 Instructions, Schedule 1, Line 21. You may be able to deduct interest you paid in 2024 on a qualified student loan. The deduction is limited to $2,500 and is phased out if your modified adjusted gross income exceeds certain limits.

docs.title: NIST SP 800-53 Revision 4: Security and Privacy Controls for Federal Information Systems and Organizations

passages.locator: Section 2.2, Table 1 (Security control identifiers and family names)
passages.text: NIST SP 800-53 Revision 4 (April 2013). Security controls are organized into eighteen families. Each family contains controls related to the general security topic of the family. The families are: Access Control (AC), Awareness and Training (AT), Audit and Accountability (AU), Security Assessment and Authorization (CA), Configuration Management (CM), Contingency Planning (CP), Identification and Authentication (IA), Incident Response (IR), Maintenance (MA), Media Protection (MP), Physical and Environmental Protection (PE), Planning (PL), Program Management (PM), Personnel Security (PS), Risk Assessment (RA), System and Services Acquisition (SA), System and Communications Protection (SC), and System and Information Integrity (SI).

NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 4, Appendix F. SA-12 SUPPLY CHAIN PROTECTION. Control: The organization protects against supply chain threats to the information system, system component, or information system service by employing organization-defined security safeguards as part of a comprehensive, defense-in-breadth information security strategy.

NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 4, Appendix J. Privacy controls are provided in a separate privacy control catalog in Appendix J, organized into eight families: Authority and Purpose (AP), Accountability, Audit, and Risk Management (AR), Data Quality and Integrity (DI), Data Minimization and Retention (DM), Individual Participation and Redress (IP), Security (SE), Transparency (TR), and Use Limitation (UL).

NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 4, Appendix F. AC-2 ACCOUNT MANAGEMENT. Control: The organization identifies and selects the types of information system accounts that support organizational missions and business functions, assigns account managers, and establishes conditions for group and role membership.

docs.title: NIST SP 800-53 Revision 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

passages.locator: Section 2.2, Table 1 (Security and privacy control families)
passages.text: NIST SP 800-53 Revision 5 (September 2020). The security and privacy controls are organized into twenty families: Access Control (AC), Awareness and Training (AT), Audit and Accountability (AU), Assessment, Authorization, and Monitoring (CA), Configuration Management (CM), Contingency Planning (CP), Identification and Authentication (IA), Incident Response (IR), Maintenance (MA), Media Protection (MP), Physical and Environmental Protection (PE), Planning (PL), Program Management (PM), Personnel Security (PS), PII Processing and Transparency (PT), Risk Assessment (RA), System and Services Acquisition (SA), System and Communications Protection (SC), System and Information Integrity (SI), and Supply Chain Risk Management (SR).

passages.locator: Chapter 3, SR family introduction; SA-12 withdrawal note
passages.text: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5. Supply chain risk management controls are consolidated in the new Supply Chain Risk Management (SR) family, beginning with SR-1 Policy and Procedures and SR-2 Supply Chain Risk Management Plan. Control SA-12 Supply Chain Protection is withdrawn and incorporated into the SR family.

NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5. This revision integrates privacy controls into the security control catalog, creating a consolidated and unified set of controls for systems and organizations. The separate privacy appendix used in the previous revision is eliminated, and privacy-specific controls appear throughout the catalog, including the new PII Processing and Transparency (PT) family.

NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5. AC-2 ACCOUNT MANAGEMENT. Control: a. Define and document the types of accounts allowed and specifically prohibited for use within the system; b. Assign account managers; c. Require organization-defined prerequisites and criteria for group and role membership.

passages.locator: Chapter 3, IA family (as originally published, September 2020)
passages.text: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5. The Identification and Authentication (IA) family contains controls IA-1 Policy and Procedures through IA-12 Identity Proofing. IA-12 requires identity proofing of users who require accounts for logical access to systems based on appropriate identity assurance level requirements.

docs.title: GSA Per Diem Rates, Fiscal Year 2024

passages.locator: FY2024 rates bulletin, standard CONUS rate
passages.text: GSA FY 2024 per diem rates, effective October 1, 2023. The standard CONUS per diem rate applies to about 2,600 counties not designated as non-standard areas. Standard lodging rate: $107 per night. Standard meals and incidental expenses (M&IE) rate: $59 per day.

GSA FY 2024 M&IE breakdown. For the $59 M&IE tier: breakfast $13, lunch $15, dinner $26, incidental expenses $5. The amount for the first and last calendar day of travel is calculated at 75 percent of the M&IE rate: $44.25.

docs.title: GSA Per Diem Rates, Fiscal Year 2025

passages.locator: FY2025 rates bulletin, standard CONUS rate
passages.text: GSA FY 2025 per diem rates, effective October 1, 2024. The standard CONUS per diem rate applies to about 2,600 counties not designated as non-standard areas. Standard lodging rate: $110 per night. Standard meals and incidental expenses (M&IE) rate: $68 per day.

GSA FY 2025 M&IE breakdown. For the $68 M&IE tier: breakfast $16, lunch $19, dinner $28, incidental expenses $5. The amount for the first and last calendar day of travel is calculated at 75 percent of the M&IE rate: $51.00.

docs.title: FM 3-0 Operations (October 2017)
docs.source_url: Army Publishing Directorate archive, FM 3-0 dated 6 October 2017

passages.text: FM 3-0, Operations, 6 October 2017. The Army's operational concept is unified land operations: the simultaneous execution of offense, defense, stability, and defense support of civil authorities across multiple domains to shape operational environments, prevent conflict, prevail in large-scale ground combat, and consolidate gains as part of unified action.

FM 3-0 (2017). The Army's strategic roles are to shape operational environments, prevent conflict, conduct large-scale ground combat, and consolidate gains. The Army accomplishes these roles as part of the joint force.

FM 3-0, Operations, 1 October 2022. This publication supersedes FM 3-0, dated 6 October 2017. Multidomain operations are the Army's contribution to joint campaigns, spanning the competition continuum. Multidomain operations replace unified land operations as the Army's operational concept.

FM 3-0 (2022). The Army's strategic roles are to shape operational environments, prevent conflict, prevail in large-scale ground combat, and consolidate gains. Army forces perform these roles as part of the joint force across the land, maritime, air, space, and cyberspace domains.

docs.title: DoD 5220.22-M National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual (NISPOM), February 28, 2006
docs.source_url: https://www.esd.whs.mil (DoD 5220.22-M, base text of February 28, 2006, before Change 1 and Change 2)

passages.text: DoD 5220.22-M, February 28, 2006. 1-201. Facility Security Officer (FSO). Contractors shall appoint a U.S. citizen employee, who is cleared as part of the facility clearance, to be the FSO to supervise and direct security measures necessary for implementing applicable requirements of this Manual.

DoD 5220.22-M, February 28, 2006. 1-202. Standard Practice Procedures. The contractor shall implement all applicable provisions of this Manual at each of its cleared facilities. Written procedures shall be prepared when the FSO believes them to be necessary for the effective implementation of this Manual. The contractor's program shall cover security education, reporting requirements, and the protection of classified information.

DoD 5220.22-M, February 28, 2006. Chapter 3. Contractors shall provide all cleared employees with security training and briefings commensurate with their involvement with classified information, including an initial security briefing before access and refresher briefings at least annually.
